profile.finding: Early Blight pattern detected on lower foliage
profile.cause: Fungal infection triggered by warm temperatures (24–29°C) and recent high moisture. Target-board circular brown spots with distinct yellow rings are actively weakening foliage photosynthesis.

prescription.marketBrands: Dithane M-45, Indofil M-45, or Chlorothalonil 75% WP
prescription.applicationWindow: Spray early morning (before 9 AM) or evening (after 5 PM) when sun is low. Cover top and underside of leaves.
prescription.preHarvestNote: Wait strictly **7 days** before harvesting any mature tomatoes.

organicAlternative.summary: **Pseudomonas fluorescens** (Bio-fungicide) @ 10g/L foliar spray + **Trichoderma harzianum** soil drenching near root collar.
organicAlternative.note: Safest option for organic certified crop plots with 0-day waiting harvest time.

sanitationSteps: Prune and immediately bag/burn infected lower leaves. Do not compost infected leaves in field edges.
Switch off overhead sprinkler systems; switch strictly to root drip lines to keep canopy leaves dry.

profile.symptom: Bright yellow powdery stripes along leaf veins
profile.finding: Yellow Rust pustules lined up in stripes on upper leaves
profile.cause: Cool nights (10–15°C) with dew or light drizzle let wind-borne rust spores germinate on wet leaves. Every stripe releases fresh spores, so untreated rust can sweep through a field within two weeks.

prescription.marketBrands: Tilt 25 EC, Bumper 25 EC, or Tebuconazole 25.9% EC (Folicur)
prescription.applicationWindow: Spray at the first sign of stripes on a dry, calm morning. Use about 200 L of spray per acre and repeat after 15 days if new stripes appear.
prescription.preHarvestNote: Stop spraying at least **30 days** before harvesting the grain.

organicAlternative.summary: **Wettable Sulphur 80% WG** @ 2g/L foliar spray + **Pseudomonas fluorescens** @ 10g/L at the first stripes.
organicAlternative.note: Slows early spread only; switch to the fungicide if stripes reach the flag leaf.

sanitationSteps: Remove volunteer wheat and grassy weeds on bunds that carry rust between seasons.
Hold back the next urea top-dressing until the rust is under control; soft, leafy growth spreads it faster.

profile.symptom: Spindle-shaped grey lesions with brown borders
profile.finding: Leaf Blast lesions detected across the upper canopy
profile.cause: Blast spreads fastest on humid nights above 90% humidity with long leaf wetness, especially where excess nitrogen has made leaves soft. Left unchecked it moves to the panicle neck and leaves chaffy, empty grain.

prescription.applicationWindow: Spray in the evening at the first leaf lesions and again at booting to protect the panicle neck. Keep 2–3 cm of standing water after spraying.
prescription.preHarvestNote: Give the last spray at least **30 days** before harvest.

organicAlternative.summary: **Pseudomonas fluorescens** @ 10g/L foliar spray + seed treatment @ 10g/kg for the next sowing.
organicAlternative.note: Works best as an early preventive spray at tillering; limited effect once neck blast starts.

sanitationSteps: Split the remaining urea into small doses and skip nitrogen top-dressing until lesions stop spreading.
Clear grassy weeds from bunds and channels; they harbour the blast fungus between crops.

profile.symptom: Tiny white winged insects and sticky honeydew under leaves
profile.finding: Whitefly colonies detected on leaf undersides
profile.cause: Hot, dry spells (30–35°C) with little rain let whitefly numbers multiply every week. They suck sap, coat leaves in honeydew and sooty mould, and can spread Cotton Leaf Curl Virus.

prescription.applicationWindow: Spray leaf undersides early in the morning when whiteflies are sluggish. Do not repeat the same insecticide group within 15 days.
prescription.preHarvestNote: Keep a gap of at least **21 days** before the next picking.

organicAlternative.summary: **Neem oil 1500 ppm** @ 5ml/L spray + **yellow sticky traps** @ 10 per acre; add **Verticillium lecanii** @ 5g/L in humid weather.
organicAlternative.note: Keeps whitefly below the damage threshold when started early, and spares pollinators.

sanitationSteps: Uproot weed hosts such as Congress grass and wild okra around the field.
Avoid synthetic pyrethroid sprays; they kill natural enemies and trigger whitefly resurgence.

profile.finding: No lesions or pest activity detected
sanitationSteps: Keep yellow sticky traps at 10 per acre to catch early whitefly flights.
Scout 20 plants a week and check leaf undersides for sucking pests.

profile.symptom: Upward leaf curling, puckering and thickened veins
profile.finding: Leaf Curl symptoms detected on young shoots
profile.cause: The virus has no cure: whiteflies pick it up from infected plants and weeds and spread it as they feed. Hot, dry weather multiplies whiteflies, so controlling them is what protects the healthy plants.
profile.climateTrigger: 33°C dry spell with active whitefly flights

prescription.marketBrands: Confidor, Tatamida SL, or Spiromesifen 22.9% SC (Oberon)
prescription.applicationWindow: Spray young shoots and leaf undersides in the evening. Rotate to a different insecticide group for the next round to avoid resistance.
prescription.preHarvestNote: Do not pick chillies for at least **40 days** after spraying.

organicAlternative.summary: **Neem Seed Kernel Extract (NSKE) 5%** spray + **yellow sticky traps** @ 12 per acre, with early rouging of curled plants.
organicAlternative.note: Cuts whitefly numbers without residues; removing infected plants stops the virus source.

sanitationSteps: Uproot and burn plants with severe curling so they stop feeding the virus to whiteflies.
Grow two border rows of maize or sorghum to block whitefly movement into the field.

profile.symptom: Reddish internal tissue with white cross-bands and a sour smell
profile.finding: Red Rot signs detected on stalk and leaf midrib
profile.cause: The fungus survives in infected setts and crop debris and travels with irrigation water. Waterlogged furrows and a susceptible variety let it rot the stalk from inside, cutting cane weight and sugar recovery.

prescription.applicationWindow: Drench the soil around healthy clumps next to infected ones. For the next crop, soak setts in the same solution for 15 minutes before planting.
prescription.preHarvestNote: Stop drenching at least **30 days** before cane harvest.

organicAlternative.summary: **Trichoderma viride** @ 2.5kg/acre mixed in farmyard manure for the furrows + sett dip in **Pseudomonas fluorescens** @ 10g/L.
organicAlternative.note: Builds soil defences for the next planting; it cannot save canes that are already rotting.

sanitationSteps: Uproot and burn infected clumps; never leave them in the field or on the bunds.
Stop irrigation water flowing out of infected patches, and do not keep this crop as a ratoon.
